analysis: Integrated across the 13 units. The PR re-routes releases. A master push now publishes staging only, gated by STAGING_ENABLED. The dev lane on master is validation-only and never published. A new release-dev-branch.yml fires on a push to `dev` and calls release-provider.yml with environment dev and `secrets: inherit`. It uses real Developer ID signing and notarization, so dev builds satisfy the self-updater's production designated requirement. The resolver (scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh) fails closed and tightens routing: a push never selects prod, and dev or staging pushes are bound to their own branch. The master verify-source gate (api.py L73-80) adds a dev-push path that needs a verified commit on dev ancestry and RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev. The tests pin these rules and add a final-app designated-requirement check, which is a tightening. Net: the new trust anchor weakens. The signing-secret trust now depends on `dev` branch protection, which the docs admit is not review-enforced. I consolidated the per-unit duplicates (units 0, 7 and 8) into one finding. Unverified: the full workflow files, the head of release-provider.yml (the 829-834 block), resolve-provider-release.sh, verify-source behavior, whether PROD_* guards hold under `secrets: inherit`, and whether the coordinator or App Attest qualification rejects dev-signed CodeDirectory hashes. The remaining platform-side acceptance of dev builds (A-017/T-054) needs a platform-owned review. The threat model has no TB for the release pipeline, so it should be updated for the dev-branch signing path.

findings.detail: The old dev lane was master-hosted: branch code was built secretless and ad-hoc signed, and publication ran master's reviewed scripts. The new .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml triggers on any push to `dev` and calls the local `./.github/workflows/release-provider.yml` with `secrets: inherit`. That reusable workflow, its actions and its scripts come from the pushed commit. The file's own header and docs/operations/provider-release.md (~L542) say `dev` has no pull_request or review rule. The master source gate (scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py L73-80) only checks for a GitHub-verified signature on dev ancestry. That proves a signature exists, not that anyone reviewed the code. Trigger: a writer on `dev`, or a compromised account with a verified signing key, edits the workflow or build scripts. Impact: exfiltration of the Apple signing, notarization and provisioning-profile secrets and of PROD_*/STAGING_* release keys. Alternatively, the attacker gets arbitrary code signed and notarized with the production Developer ID (team SLDQ2GJ6TL, io.darkbloom.provider) that the self-updater's production designated requirement accepts. Both weaken the trusted-binary registry and build-qualification chain. Fix: require a pull_request and review ruleset on `dev` before enabling the trigger. Move the Apple and release secrets into protected environments that a dev ref cannot read, and pass explicit DEV_* secrets instead of `secrets: inherit`. Pin the reusable workflow to master or a SHA.
findings.title: Unreviewed push to `dev` runs the pushed workflow with inherited Developer ID, notarization and release secrets
